questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.learningObjective: Identify when a group misreads private beliefs
questions.stem: A ticket notes the team nods in standup but privately doubts the deadline.

options.text: Each member thinks others are confident, so all stay silent.
No one privately doubts the deadline.
The team truly believes the deadline is fine.
options.misconception: confuses public agreement with private belief

questions.explanation: Pluralistic ignorance occurs when individuals privately reject a norm but assume others accept it, so no one speaks up. The tempting idea that the team truly agrees fails because private doubts exist.
questions.hint: Look for private rejection with public silence.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.learningObjective: Apply availability heuristic to recent events

stimulus.body: A bar chart shows bug reports spike after a recent outage. Engineers estimate risk from memory of that outage.

questions.stem: Given the chart, engineers overestimate bug risk because recent events come to mind easily.

options.misconception: confuses similarity with ease of recall

options.text: They anchor on the first bug report.

questions.explanation: The availability heuristic judges likelihood by how easily examples come to mind. The tempting representativeness idea fails because similarity is not the driver here.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.stem: Design a ticket experiment where devs advocate a tool they dislike for low pay.

answer.exemplar: Randomly assign developers to write a positive review of a disliked tool for either one dollar or twenty dollars, then measure their later attitude toward the tool; low-pay participants should shift attitudes more to reduce dissonance.

questions.explanation: Low payment creates insufficient justification, producing attitude change to reduce dissonance. The tempting idea that high pay drives change fails because ample pay explains the behavior.

questions.stem: Explain why cross-team pairing may reduce prejudice between frontend and backend devs.

questions.explanation: Equal-status contact with shared goals reduces prejudice. The tempting mere-contact idea fails because unstructured contact can reinforce stereotypes.
